messages:
Mark this whole submitted practice essay out of 100 using the synthetic course rubric in the fixture. Use all four allocations and tell me the material weaknesses.

City councils should ban private cars from the centre. In our supplied trial record, nitrogen dioxide fell from 44 to 31 micrograms per cubic metre between September and October after the trial began. This proves that the ban caused the fall and will keep air equally clean in every season. An objection is that winter deliveries and disabled residents need access. That is only a convenience, so it has no force. A permit scheme is another option, but a ban must be better because a ban removes all cars. Weather was windier in October and the traffic counter was broken, but the pollution numbers are real. Therefore every council should make the same permanent ban. The trial is relevant because it measured the outcome that matters. Cleaner air benefits residents, and a policy that reduces exposure deserves consideration.
expected_facts: Rubric allocates Argument40/Objections30/Evidence20/Clarity10. The essay has causal, seasonal and cross-city overextensions; unweighed access objections; unsupported comparison to permits; a relevant outcome measure and readable structure. Exact score is judgment, not an answer key.

messages: I need a static tip-deflection estimate. Ideal rigidly clamped cantilever, transverse point load 1000 N at the free end, length 480 mm, solid rectangle 40 mm wide and 120 mm deep in the bending direction. Homogeneous isotropic linear elastic material E=200 GPa, nu=0.30, G=E/[2(1+nu)], shear factor kappa=5/6. Small deflection and elastic behaviour are stipulated. My accuracy budget permits at most 2% error from omitting shear, measured relative to bending-plus-shear deflection. Is Euler-Bernoulli adequate for that budget? Please decide and show a compact check.
I copied the bending depth incorrectly: it is 24 mm, not 120 mm. All other stipulated assumptions and the 2% budget stay the same. Does your decision change?
expected_facts: At h=.12,L=.48, r=delta_s/delta_b=.04875, omission/total=.0464839094: fails 2%. At h=.024 r=.00195, omission/total=.0019462049: meets 2%. This is only a shear-omission model budget, not a physical accuracy guarantee.

messages: For a simply supported beam I need midspan static deflection under one central transverse force of 2000 N. L=1.2 m; solid rectangle b=40 mm, bending depth h=120 mm. messages: I'm estimating static tip deflection of an ideal clamped solid rectangular beam under a 500 N transverse tip load. L=.8 m, b=.04 m, E=200 GPa, nu=.30, G=E/[2(1+nu)], kappa=5/6. expected_facts: r=.78(h/L)^2; 1% threshold h<=L sqrt[(.01/.99)/.78], about .09104 m. The supplied interval straddles threshold: cannot settle. Measure bending-direction depth h, not width, load or unknown tolerance.

messages: Mechanics habit I know: test an assumption by comparing predictions. Help me use it on this actual history claim: 'The new toll caused the merchants to protest in June.' My evidence is a merchants' petition dated June 2 demanding repeal of the toll introduced in May. A guild election dispute also began in May. Show me one move on my claim, name what history requires, and give me one short thing to try.
I found a letter by the petition organizers dated April 20 planning the June protest over the guild election, before the toll existed. Does that overturn the original claim?
expected_facts: Petition supports toll as a stated grievance, not exclusive or initiating cause. Election dispute is rival explanation. History needs source date/authorship/context/representativeness and discriminating chronology. April letter weakens toll-as-origin claim but does not exclude later toll contribution or all merchant motives.

messages: Can I carry the mechanics habit 'check the limiting case' into this history paragraph? 'After the harbour opened, exports doubled, so the harbour alone caused the increase.' My only evidence is the port's annual export ledger. The same year a trade embargo ended. I want an example using my sentence, not a list of study habits. I haven't tried this unaided.
expected_facts: An alternative embargo explanation challenges sole causation. A comparison port affected by embargo but not new harbour, or dated commodity/route records, could discriminate with stated limitations. Historical context, dates/provenance/comparability must be independently supported; numerical limiting procedure does not mechanically prove historical cause.
